what: repro/lfm25-24b-a2b-q8-b70 (v4: exact fusions, the steadier prompt-path conversion, and prompt steps of 2,048 tokens run as 512-token pieces) built by its build.sh (fresh upstream clone + the aggregate patch) and run by its serve.sh/check.sh on card 1 of the lab host, Gemma on card 0; registered in experiments/lfm25-24b-a2b-b70/notes/2026-10-14-lfm25-24b-a2b-bringup.md before running

logprob_probe_fast_b_vs_r0.what: top-8 log-probabilities of every step, 12 suite prompts x 96 tokens, bit-identical to the lab reference R0 (probe-reference-r0.json)

long_prompt_probe_fast_b_vs_r0.what: same check on three long prompts of about 2K, 8K and 24K tokens (lab text, not published), 128 tokens each

edge_prompts_fast_b_vs_unfused.what: raw token prompts cut from the 24K lab prompt to 513, 516, 520, 1029, 1543, 2047, 2048, 2049, 2052, 2056, 4103, 6151 and 8200 tokens (the last 512-token piece 1-8 tokens long in several), 64 tokens, top-8 log-probabilities; fast (2,048-token steps in 512-token pieces) vs unfused (512-token steps)

suite: repro/qwen36-27b-autoround-int4-b70/realistic-suite-v1.json (12 prompts, six classes, 512 tokens, greedy, seed 42, cache_prompt false); metric = median over the six classes of each class median tok/s for tokens 1-100 after TTFT

server_prompt_rate.what: prompt reading speed as llama-server reports it (timings.prompt_per_second), one user, prompt cache off, after the server has answered other requests; the three long prompts (lab text, not published) each twice
server_prompt_rate.why_v4_is_faster: serve.sh fast now reads prompts in 2,048-token steps (-ub 2048) and runs every matrix product, expert product and attention of a step as 512-token pieces (LLAMA_SYCL_PREFILL_SLICE=512, LLAMA_SYCL_PREFILL_SLICE_FA=1), each with the shape, rows and key count of the 512-token step it replaces, so the results are the same bytes; each weight is converted to 16-bit once per step instead of four times

sweep.command: llama-bench -ngl 99 -fa 1 -ctk f16 -ctv f16 -b 2048 -ub 2048 -t 8 --poll 50 -p 2048 -n 128 -d 0,2048,4096,8192,16384,32768 -r 3 -o json, environment of serve.sh fast
sweep.note: pp and tg alternate, so every pp point after depth 0 runs on weights a decode step has reordered, as in a server
